items.title: DSM categories don't always carve nature at the joints
items.claim: The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual is the standard US classification of mental disorders. What's the standard critique?

options.text: DSM categories perfectly match underlying biology

Categories were chosen by committee consensus; high comorbidity between disorders, dimensional features within categories, and biological heterogeneity all suggest DSM may not reflect natural kinds. The NIH RDoC (Research Domain Criteria, 2010) proposes a dimensional alternative for research
DSM has only one category for all disorders

items.reveal:
DSM-5 (2013) maintained categorical diagnosis under pressure to introduce dimensional aspects. Thomas Insel (then NIMH director) announced in 2013 that NIMH would 're-orient' research away from DSM categories toward RDoC.

Key problems: ~60% of patients meet criteria for two or more disorders simultaneously; treatment response often crosses diagnostic boundaries; genetic studies (Cross-Disorder Group, 2013) show overlapping risk variants across disorders.

ICD-11 (WHO, 2022) introduced some dimensional elements.
items.why: Diagnostic categories shape research, insurance and stigma. The categories matter clinically even where their scientific basis is questioned.

items.title: The Health Belief Model predicts (some) preventive behaviours
items.claim: Rosenstock's 1974 Health Belief Model proposes that preventive behaviour depends on perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits and barriers. What's its empirical track record?

options.text: It predicts all health behaviours perfectly

Meta-analyses (Carpenter 2010) find modest predictive power: perceived barriers strongest, perceived benefits moderate, susceptibility and severity weaker. The model under-weights social and emotional factors
It only applies to dental hygiene

items.reveal:
Rosenstock developed the HBM from 1950s public health work on TB screening uptake. It has been applied to vaccination, screening, smoking cessation and COVID behaviours.

Competitors and extensions: Theory of Planned Behavior (Ajzen 1991, adds intention and perceived control); Transtheoretical Model (Prochaska 1979, stages of change). Behavioural economics (EAST framework: easy, attractive, social, timely) is the more recent UK policy framework.
items.why: Behaviour-change theories provide testable frameworks but rarely explain more than a fraction of variance. Combining them with structural interventions usually outperforms either alone.

items.title: Choking is more than just nerves
items.claim: Sian Beilock and colleagues' research on choking under pressure identifies two mechanisms. Which?

options.text: Distraction (anxiety occupies working memory needed for the task) and explicit monitoring (conscious attention to automatic motor skills disrupts them) — different mechanisms suggest different interventions

items.reveal:
Beilock and Carr (2001, 2005) showed expert golfers putted worse when paying conscious attention to their swing; novices benefited from explicit instruction.

Distraction-based choking responds to attention training and pre-performance routines; monitoring-based choking responds to maintaining flow-state distraction (focusing on external targets rather than mechanics). The dual-process model has reshaped elite athlete preparation.
items.why: Choking has identifiable mechanisms with specific countermeasures. Generic 'stay calm' advice misses both.
